plain_text:
CITY OF BRISTOL, CONNECTICUT 
COMMISSION ON AGING MEETING 
Thursday, September 17, 2026 - Regular Meeting Minutes 
Bristol Senior Center – 240 Stafford Avenue 
Bristol, CT 06010 – Phone: 860-584-7895 Room #109   
 
Present: Commissioners: Larry Zbikowski, Cathy Duck, Ellen McCusker, Chris Leigh, Dolores 
Ricker, Frank Peronace, Executive Director Jason Krueger, Assistant Director Taylor Maghini, and 
Council Liaison Susan Tyler. 
  
Absent: Commissioners: Sheila Herens 
 
Meeting Called to order: Commissioner Larry Zbikowski called the meeting to order at 11:02am 
 
Approval of Minutes: Commissioner Duck moved to accept the minutes from the June 18, 2026 
Meeting, seconded by Commissioner Leigh, All in Favor.  
 
Public Participation: None 
 
Council Update: Council Liaison Tyler updated the commission about a special City Council Meeting 
on September 22nd to discuss the purchase of Chipanee Golf Course and a vote may follow. Council 
Liaison Tyler also informed the commission that the Ordinance Committee is going to be reviewing the 
“Homestead Act”. This is a possible tax credit for single family homeowners. Council Liaison Tyler let 
the commission know that City emails were hacked, but are now back up and running. 
 
Correspondence: Assistant Director Maghini shared with the commission a thank you letter from 
Komanetsky Estates, a letter from the City Clerks office approving our changes to policies and 
procedures, and lastly a letter from Bristol Health thanking us for the donation of $7,500 to the Bristol 
Hospital Foundation in support of our Foot Clinic. 
 
Unfinished, “Old” Business: Executive Director Krueger informed the commission that the new 
Policies and Procedures were approved by Corp. Council and the new Rules and Regulations will be 
posted around the center.  
 
Executive Director Krueger gave an update on the parking lot project. We are still waiting on the top 
coat and then it will be paved all the way up to Stafford Ave. Lights, signs, and bollards are in the 
process of being installed. Executive Director Krueger let the commission that the Health Department 
construction is projected to be complete by the end of January.  
 
New Business: Executive Director Krueger informed the commission that the center will be 
conducting a building use survey for the month of October, since the last one conducted was 3 years 
ago. There will be physical copies and a QR code for an online survey.  
 
Commissioner Duck inquired about the snow removal service that the City of Bristol was working on 
for Seniors and Disabled residents. Executive Director Krueger informed the commission that it is still 
being worked out in the Mayors Office.
Any other business:  
 
Executive Director Krueger reported the statistics for June, 2026, we had 6,626 participants, total 
membership was 6,252, with 9 deceased, and 48 new members. Our fundraiser total for 2025-26 ended 
at $24,329.00. Statistics for July, 2026, we had 5,455 participants, total membership was 6,264, with 22 
deceased, and 28 new members, and our fundraiser letters were being prepped to send out for 2026-27. 
The statistics for August, 2026, we had 5,639 participants, total membership was 6,328, with 10 
deceased, and 49 new members. Our fundraiser total for 2026-27 is $22,798.47.  
 
Executive Director Krueger stated that our upcoming events include a Pasta Supper Fundraiser 
on September 23rd, a Candidate Meet & Greet on October 7th, a Craft Fair on October 23rd and 
24th, and we will be hosting a Citizen’s Academy for the City on October 7th.  
 
Adjournment: Commissioner Ricker moved “to adjourn” at 11:24 a.m., seconded by Commissioner 
Leigh.  All in favor. 
 
Respectfully Submitted, 
Taylor Maghini – Secretary to The Commission
